author: Russell Brand
description:
A discussion sparked by the swearing-in of a Muslim mayor in Brighton explores what national identity, religion, and public authority even mean in a country that is officially secular yet historically Christian. The conversation moves through monarchy, migration, cultural cohesion, and the tension between organic social change and top-down ideological enforcement, questioning whether diversity is emerging naturally or being imposed as a substitute for a shared moral framework. Beneath it all sits a deeper concern: when faith, nationhood, and meaning are hollowed out, power doesn’t disappear — it simply reappears in new, less accountable forms.
